clue.text: Setter's right out of sweetener for drink

parts.note: the setter speaking of themself: I am, shortened to I'm

indicators.note: right taken out of the next word, so its R is dropped

parts.note: a bribe is a payment that sweetens someone

explanation.surface: A setter declines to put sugar in a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To imbibe is to drink, especially alcohol; the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: For a start, noblesse oblige is violated and that's disgraceful

indicators.note: something violated is broken, so the letters are rearranged
for a start means take only the opening letter of noblesse

explanation.surface: Breaking the principle of noblesse oblige is shameful.
explanation.walkthrough: Noblesse oblige is the idea that privilege brings duty.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignoble means dishonourable or base, so disgraceful is a close synonym.

clue.text: Barks heard and almost felt

indicators.note: heard tells us the bark word is spoken

parts.note: a hound bays, a deep bark

explanation.surface: Dog barks are heard and nearly felt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'felt' looks like a verb but is the fabric noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Baize is a woollen cloth like felt, used on card and snooker tables.

clue.text: I don't approve of this rest treatment as a provider of energy

parts.note: boo is a cry of disapproval

indicators.note: treatment means the letters are worked on and rearranged

explanation.surface: A patient objects to rest as therapy, wanting an energy boost.
explanation.definitionFit: A booster is anything that boosts, such as a vitamin shot or rocket stage that adds energy.

clue.text: Stole back to cover a quarrel

indicators.note: to cover means the turned word goes round the next piece, enclosing it
back tells us to read the wrap word from its end to its start

parts.note: a stole is a scarf-like wrap worn round the shoulders

explanation.surface: Someone returns a stolen item to hide a row, or a stole is put back over a dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stole' looks like a verb (thieved) but is the noun: a SCARF, which 'back' turns into FRACS before it covers A.
explanation.definitionFit: A fracas is a noisy disturbance or brawl, close in meaning to a quarrel.

clue.text: They are found in the belfry, same as dead

definitions.text: They are found in the belfry
definitions.meaning: people who pull the bells in a church tower
dead ... means exact lookalikes, so the word alone means the same as with dead

explanation.surface: Bellringers in a tower are as good as dead.
explanation.definitionFit: Bell-pullers are ringers; and a ringer, dead or not, is a lookalike.

clue.text: Blokes take a long time gathering right gooseberries

indicators.note: take means the men word takes the next pieces inside

parts.note: blokes are chaps

indicators.note: gathering means the long time word gathers the next letter inside

parts.note: an eon is a long age

explanation.surface: Men spend ages picking the best gooseberries.
explanation.walkthrough: A gooseberry is British slang for an unwanted third person with a couple, like a chaperon.
explanation.definitionFit: Playing gooseberry means accompanying a courting couple, as chaperons once did.

clue.text: A bit postmenopausal, tired and cross

indicators.note: a bit means a piece taken from inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A woman is somewhat past menopause, tired and irritable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like 'angry' but is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A saltire is a diagonal X-shaped cross, as on the Scottish flag.

clue.text: Sexy dog as a substitute for old lover? That's obscene

indicators.note: the dog word replaces the former partner inside sexy

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
a mutt is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: Someone gets a sexy dog to replace a former lover, which is vulgar.
explanation.definitionFit: Smutty means dirty or indecent, the same as obscene.

clue.text: Green with envy welcoming press people of stature at match

indicators.note: welcoming means the word envy takes the following pieces into its middle

parts.note: people who press clothes with an iron: ironmen
someone of stature is tall
a friendly is a match played for no competitive stake

explanation.surface: Someone jealous watches tall pressmen at a football match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'press people' look like journalists but are people who press clothes with an iron. 'Green' is the environmental sense, not the colour of envy.
explanation.definitionFit: Green in the ecological sense describes products and practices that do little harm to nature.

clue.text: Say nothing

parts.note: split the last word: to say no is to protest, and a thing is an item, both senses of one word

explanation.surface: An instruction to stay silent.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'nothing' as 'no' plus 'thing': the verb meaning to say no and the noun meaning a thing are the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to protest or say no; as a noun it means an article or thing, so it covers both halves.

clue.text: Within that location round Maidenhead you'll find an instrument

indicators.note: round means the place word goes around the next piece

parts.note: therein means in that place
the head, or first letter, of Maiden is M

explanation.surface: A tip that a musical instrument can be found somewhere near the Berkshire town of Maidenhead.
explanation.walkthrough: Maidenhead is a town west of London, but here it means the head of 'Maiden'. 'Within' is not an insertion signal; it belongs to the phrase for THEREIN.
explanation.definitionFit: The theremin is an electronic instrument played without touch, by moving the hands near two antennas.

clue.text: Danger across the Channel, I send up love first

parts.note: in France, across the English Channel, the word for I is je

indicators.note: first tells us the zero letter is moved to the front of the mocking word

parts.note: a send-up is a parody
love is zero in tennis, written as O

explanation.surface: Someone in France mocks love before anything else and courts danger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I' across the Channel is French; 'send up' is the noun for a mocking imitation, whose love-letter 'first' brings to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeopardy means peril or risk of harm, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Frenchman's confirmed short visit

definitions.note: possessive adjective, matching the adjective for southern France

parts.note: something confirmed is proven

indicators.note: short means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: to call on someone is to visit

explanation.surface: A Frenchman's quick visit has been confirmed.
explanation.definitionFit: Provençal describes what belongs to Provence, so a Frenchman from there has Provençal things.

clue.text: See 23
Wrap organs for transplantation

indicators.note: organs for transplantation are moved around, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Organs are wrapped ready for a transplant operation.
explanation.definitionFit: A sarong is a length of cloth wrapped around the body, so it is a wrap garment.

clue.text: Dimwit hairy chef made to strip

indicators.note: stripping removes the outsides, leaving the middle of each word

explanation.surface: A foolish hirsute cook is made to undress.
explanation.definitionFit: An airhead is slang for a stupid person, so a dimwit.

clue.text: Real blessing for D?

parts.note: the letter D is the end of the word for the deity

explanation.surface: A cryptic question about the letter D as a gift.
explanation.walkthrough: The letter D finishes the word God, so D is God's end.
explanation.definitionFit: A godsend is an unexpected stroke of luck, a true blessing.

clue.text: A plea for help to secure finest material

indicators.note: to secure means the distress call holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: SOS is the distress signal
the finest is the best

explanation.surface: A cry for help to get hold of the best fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Asbestos is a fibrous mineral once widely used as a fire-resistant building material.

clue.text: Regardless of 5th Avenue?

parts.note: read as 'a New York': the indefinite article plus NY, the abbreviation for the city where Fifth Avenue runs
an avenue is a way, a road

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether Fifth Avenue matters at all.
explanation.walkthrough: Fifth Avenue is a famous New York street, so it is 'a NY way'.
explanation.definitionFit: Anyway and regardless both mean nevertheless, whatever the circumstances.

clue.text: Father under secure hospital in the city

indicators.note: under means the father word is placed after the earlier pieces in this down clue

parts.note: to bag something is to secure it
dad is father

explanation.surface: A father is held in a secure hospital in town.
explanation.definitionFit: Baghdad is the capital city of Iraq.

clue.text: Source of fruit or veg

parts.note: chard is a leafy vegetable

explanation.surface: Asking where fruit or vegetables come from.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchard is a plantation of fruit trees, where fruit comes from.

clue.text: See 9
Butchers grill Aberdeen cattle topsides and rumps

indicators.note: topside and rump are cuts of beef, here the first and last letters of each word

explanation.surface: Butchers cook Aberdeen Angus cattle cuts such as topside and rump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butchers' is rhyming slang: butcher's hook means look. Aberdeen Angus is a Scottish beef breed.
explanation.definitionFit: In Cockney rhyming slang a butcher's is a look, and a glance is a quick look.

clue.text: How reprisal affected Mayflower's precursor?

indicators.note: affected means changed, so the letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: How did retaliation affect the forerunner of the Pilgrim ship Mayflower?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mayflower' suggests the Pilgrim ship, but read it as May flower: the proverb says spring rains bring May flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: In the rhyme, spring rain in the fourth month comes before the flowers of May.

clue.text: A sweet complexion

definitions.meaning: a summer dessert of fruit with dairy
a fair, rosy skin is described with this phrase

explanation.surface: Someone has a lovely skin tone.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a pudding and also a smooth pink-and-white skin tone.

clue.text: Lead up the garden path in Giverny of 8, so to speak

indicators.note: so to speak tells us the French-and-English pair is said out loud

parts.note: in Giverny, in France, 'of' is de; 8 is SMUTTY, meaning lewd

explanation.surface: Someone misleads a visitor on a path in Monet's garden at Giverny.
explanation.walkthrough: Giverny is Monet's garden village in France. 8 points to 8 down: SMUTTY = LEWD.
explanation.definitionFit: To lead someone up the garden path is an idiom for deceiving them.

clue.text: Prepared to ride topless in a confused state

indicators.note: topless means the first letter is removed

parts.note: a horse prepared to ride has been saddled

explanation.surface: Someone gets ready to ride without a top, while muddled.
explanation.definitionFit: Addled means muddled or confused in mind, matching the phrase.
